newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil supports call for emergency coffee meeting.
newsitem.headline: Brazil supports call for emergency coffee meeting.

text.p: Brazil supports a request by African coffee producing countries to hold an extraordinary meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), said a top Brazil coffee government official.

But Brazil has no position on a proposal by African nations for further cuts in world coffee exports in the first half of 1997, which the Africans wish to propose at the special meeting, said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce ministry.
"We agree that there should be an extraordinary meeting of the ACPC," Assis told Reuters after a meeting today with a delegation led by Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze.

At the meeting Gauze spoke of the African nations' concern over the international world market situation and gave a summary of talks held earlier this week with Colombian coffee officials, Assis said.
After the meetings in Bogota, officials released a statement saying they had agreed on a need to cut exports by ACPC member countries by a further 2.5 million 60-kg bags in the first half of 1997.
However Assis said that Brazil could not comment on the proposal at this time.
"We have no position for the time being. We are going to study it," he said.
Assis said that the time and the place of the emergency meeting would depend on ACPC officials.
But he added "it will probably be in Rio de Janeiro during the period of the January seminar".

An international coffee seminar is to be held in Rio de Janeiro on January 20-22 with speakers scheduled to include Assis, top Colombian coffee official Jorge Cardenas and ACPC secretary-general Roberio Silva.
